reply_data.bodyHTML:
Note

I don’t think pattern matching can do this without drawbacks.

I suppose this is what you want:

  1. Easy
MiniHipatterns.setup({
  highlighters = {
    todo = { pattern = { --[["TODO",]] "TODO_TODO", "TODO_TODO_TODO", --[[...]] }, group = "MiniHipatternsHack" },
  },
})
  1. Hard
MiniHipatterns.setup({
  highlighters = {
    todo = {
      pattern = { "TODO_", "_TODO" },
      group = function(b, m, d)
        local line = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_lines(b, d.line - 1, d.line, true)[1]
        local range = { d.from_col, d.to_col }
        if m == "_TODO" then
          local left = line:sub(range[1] - #m + 1, range[1])
          if not left:match("TODO_") then return nil end
        end
        if m == "TODO_" then
          local right = line:sub(range[2], range[2] + #m - 1)
          if not right:match("_TODO") then return nil end
        end
        return "MiniHipatternsHack"
      end,
    },
  },
})

comment_data.body:
> So the first pattern matches, the second also matches, but I would expect the first pattern to re-match for the _middle_ `TODO_` as well 🤔

The core reason for the expectation mismatch is indeed how several pattern matches on a single line is done. The current approach works like this:
- Find full match of the *whole pattern* (not only intended submatch). Register pattern's (sub)match.
- Keep looking for the next pattern match [starting from the right of the full match](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/7d6fcfd879fe520aba187fe2bd25078fa2367d03/lua/mini/hipatterns.lua#L941).

This is how Neovim's search (like with `/`) works. With a string of many `-`, searching for `--` will not result into overlapping matches.

What would make this use case work with a single `TODO_TODO` pattern is to keep looking starting from the right of the whole initial **match start**.

In theory, this is a very trivial change of `to + 1` into `from + 1`. But I think this was not done initially to 1) "be more like regular search matches"; and 2) performance reasons (each line part is searched only once). There might have been some edge cases also, but they are at least not in the tests.

I'll take a closer look at what is the best compromise here. An alternative approach is to keep looking fro the right of the *real match*. At least it makes it work with the patterns in the original comment.

reply_data.body: Hola beloved author! Thanks a lot for replying 🙏 > This is how Neovim's search (like with /) works. With a string of many -, searching for -- will not result into overlapping matches. This is true, but is _not_ the same thing as what I'm trying to do. What I'm trying to do is known in regex world as positive lookahead & lookbehind, which exists in vim-regex but not in Lua patterns. Your plugin, via the `before()...()after` syntax basically emulate this mechanism in Lua, but fails to consider the whole match as only the `...` part but instead considers the whole match to be `before...after`. The equivalent vim-regex for my overlapping search Lua pattern `()TODO_()TODO_` is really `TODO_\zeTODO_`, meaning: > I want to match `TODO_` only when it's followed by another `TODO_`. Which when tried using regular (neo)vim search on `TODO_TODO_TODO_something` will match twice as expected for the first two `TODO_`: (orange is my current match under the cursor, and yellow is the other match) And that's why I had the remaining `_TODO_()TODO()_[^T][^O]` to match on the third one, meaning: > I want to match `TODO` only if its preceeded by `_TODO_`, followed by `_` and 2 chars that are not `TO` --- About performance, it would only impact when there are a lot of lookahead/lookbehind patterns, but I don't think it'd impact that much in practice. And if it actually does, a simple note in checkhealth and/or in the documentation around this mechanism could be enough I think 🤔

reply_data.body:
> > Using `from + 1` (which I initially suggested and was wondering about performance) would impact performance of _every_ highlighter that uses Lua patterns.
> 
> I don't really understand how it would impact the normal ones, but I guess you're much more knowledgable about your own plugin `¯\_(ツ)_/¯`

Let's say there is a pattern `xxx` and a line "Three xxx Four xxxx". The matching will be like this:
- Find first `xxx` match. It is from 7 to 9 characters. Register it.
- Keep searching matches starting from character 9+1=10. Find the match at the start of "xxxx" (16-18). Register it.
- Keep searching starting from character 18+1=19. No matches.

With `from+1` it will be:
- Find first `xxx` match. It is from 7 to 9 characters. Register it.
- Keep searching matches starting from character **7+1=8** (i.e. two extra characters are searched again). Find the match at the start of "xxxx" (16-18). Register it.
- Keep searching starting from character **16+1=17**. Find a match at 17-19. Register it.
- Keep searching starting from character 17+1=18. There is none.

Every match with the `from + 1` approach leads to `<pattern-length> - 1` extra characters searched (via `string.find()`). This might not sound like much, but many highlighters times many matches it *might* get visible. Not even speaking about the change in behavior here.

The "... keep looking from the right of the real match" approach will act like `to + 1` case here (as real match is the full match), and will only differ if the right end of real match is earlier than the right end of full match. Which probably should be okay.

The basis of my idea is to pre-process the pattern to see if it's a plain `xxx` or a pattern with submatches

Then for the hot loop:
- for plain patterns: use current matching and advancement
- for patterns with lookbehind, advance `from +1`
- for other patterns, advance `sub_to +1`
